messages:
ana: Quick sync — I pushed a draft tweak to continuous-batching for private clusters. Trying a queue-priority bias when KV cache pressure > 0.7 to prefer short prefix joins and avoid giant KV-miss batches. Anyone with cycles to sanity-check?

matt: ack, saw the PR. Curious how you measure "KV cache pressure" — is that per-GPU or global for the node pool?

ana: typo — ana :) It's computed per-device as cached_kv_tokens / max_kv_tokens (rolling 30s). We saw pathological batches where many requests with cold prefixes grouped and produced huge GPU memory spikes.

jing: can you paste the config? want to see thresholds and whether it's opt-in for private overrides only

ana: sure, snippet from the override we tested in staging: ```
private.batch.queue_policy: "priority_bias"
private.batch.kv_pressure_threshold: 0.7
private.batch.token_budget_target: 1200  # tokens per batch target for biased queues
private.batch.kernel_fallback: "auto"  # try fp16 -> int8 fallback on OOM
```

matt: looks reasonable. Two quick questions: (1) token_budget_target looks high for constrained 8GB VPC GPUs, are these tests on 32GB machines? (2) kernel_fallback auto — does it switch kernels mid-batch or require a retry?

ana: good points. Tests so far were on a small private pool with 16GB cards (nvlink disabled by policy). The heuristic clamps token_budget_target down based on device_mem_free and model_quant_profile. Fallback currently triggers as a retry path: the serving runtime catches OOM and retries the same batch with alternate kernel/quant path. That adds latency but avoids catastrophic failures.

perf-bot: perf/regression: staging run 1766782300 -> p50 +18ms, p95 +120ms when priority_bias enabled, but tail failures dropped from 3->0 (OOMs). Link: https://perf.redwood/staging/1766782300

oliver: That's promising — reduction in failures is good. Can we reduce p95 impact by limiting max_retries and doing preflight estimate? Maybe estimate token footprint before batching and split when estimated > device capacity.

ana: yes, preflight estimate is next. Current queue_policy computes an estimated_token_sum per potential batch and rejects formation if > mem_budget_estimate. Problem was mem_budget_estimate was conservative and didn't account for KV cache sharing benefits. So we biased to prefer smaller batches when pressure high which reduced OOMs but increased latency.

jing: idea: maintain two queues — hot-prefix queue (high priority, small target token budget ~200) and bulk queue (lower priority, larger budget when cache pressure low). On enqueue, compute prefix_hotness score and route. This allows short interactive requests to get fast join without polluting bulk.

matt: that's basically what we prototyped ages ago. Differences: need deterministic fairness so bulk isn't starved. Suggest a token-leaky bucket that drains bulk quota periodically. Also add a guard to force kernel_fallback attempt only for batches > X tokens to avoid spamming retries for tiny batches.

ana: agreed. I'll add bulk_token_quota and hot_quota config: ```
private.batch.hot_target: 220
private.batch.bulk_target: 1600
private.batch.bulk_quota_per_sec: 8000
private.batch.retries.max: 2
private.batch.fallback_min_tokens: 800
```

perf-bot: quick compare after new flags: staging 1766782500 -> p50 +6ms, p95 +45ms, error rate 0.1% (was 0.8%). CPU on the host increased slightly due to extra routing logic.

sre-bot: note: on constrained hardware (8GB) the scheduler should default to passthrough mode (no batching) unless explicit customer override. Need to ensure private default respects that.

ana: putting that on the checklist for the rollout doc. Plan: feature-gate priority_bias for private clusters, default off for any node with device_mem < 12GB. Document per-customer override path in console and terraform provider.

oliver: one more: kernel selection heuristics — can we include a cheap microprofile before first token to choose optimal kernel (attention kernel with smaller seq optimizations vs general)? Maybe use a 1-2 token dry run estimate using existing KV shape to pick kernel without full retry.

matt: cheap but adds complexity. Another option: maintain a small LRU of (model_id, seq_len_range) -> preferred_kernel inferred from recent successful batches. Use it as hint for new batches.

ana: love that. I'll wire a kernel_preference cache and tie eviction to model updates. Okay, I'll update the PR with: dual-queue routing, bulk quotas, fallback_min_tokens, kernel_pref cache, and rollout gating by device_mem. Thanks for the checks.

jing: thanks — happy to review the PR later today. :thumbsup:

matt: +1. Can we add an opt-in flag for customers "private.batch.experimental_priority_bias" so support can roll it out to specific accounts?

ana: will add. scheduling a canary rollout to 5 customers tomorrow.

perf-bot: FYI scheduled perf job for canary run 1766790000

ana: sweet. I'll post results in this thread when available.
